instructions: Rinse the 1 1/2 cups rice until the water runs clear. Put it in a pot with 2 1/4 cups water, bring it to a boil, then cover, turn the heat to low and cook for 15 minutes. Take it off the heat and leave the lid on until you're ready to eat.
Meanwhile, whisk 3 tbsp fish sauce and 2 tbsp brown sugar with 1/3 cup water until the sugar dissolves.
Finely chop the onion and mince the 4 garlic cloves. Thinly slice 3 green onions and chop about 1/4 cup of cilantro.
Peel and devein the 1 1/2 lbs shrimp if they aren't already, and pat them very dry. Sprinkle 1/4 tsp of the pepper over them.

Heat 2 tbsp of the oil in a large skillet over high until it shimmers. Add half the shrimp in a single layer and leave them for 1 minute, until the undersides are pink with a few browned spots. Flip them and cook the other side for 30 seconds, then move them to a plate. They'll still be a little see-through in the middle. Do the rest the same way.
Turn the heat to medium and add the last 1 tbsp oil and the onion. Cook for about 5 minutes, stirring now and then, until soft and see-through.
Add the garlic and stir for 30 seconds, until you can smell it. Don't let it brown.
Pour in the fish sauce mixture and turn the heat up to medium high. Let it bubble for 2 to 3 minutes, scraping up the browned bits, until it's reduced to a dark, glossy syrup that coats the spoon.
Tip the shrimp and their juices back in and toss them in the sauce for 1 to 2 minutes, until the sauce is sticky and clings to them and the shrimp are white all the way through.
Take the pan off the heat and stir in the green onions, the cilantro and the last 1/4 tsp pepper. Put the 1/2 tsp red pepper flakes in a small bowl for the table.
Taste the sauce. If it's flat, add a few drops more fish sauce.
Serve over the rice, with the red pepper flakes on the side.
method_notes: All three read versions cook shrimp in a fish sauce and sugar sauce with garlic and finish with green onion, served with plain rice. Once Upon a Chef, the lead, dissolves dark brown sugar in fish sauce and water instead of making a caramel, softens onion and garlic, cooks peeled shrimp and simmers them in the thin sauce, finishing with green onion and cilantro. Wok and Kin and Vicky Pham cook shell-on shrimp the traditional way, marinate them with garlic, shallot, bouillon powder and black pepper, and cook them until the sugar caramelizes and the sauce is nearly gone; Wok and Kin adds dark soy and puts the fish sauce in last. This one follows the lead's sauce but sears the shrimp first and reduces the sauce to a sticky glaze before they go back in.
